Alternatively, if wanting to deploy it now, it still should be cast pre-combat since it has haste, but plotting is likely better given the hand full of tricks.

annotations.description: Discarded a basic Island while severely mana-screwed with only 1 land on the battlefield. With 3 lands in an 8-card hand and desperate need for mana development, every land is critical. Enduring Curiosity (4 mana, already one in graveyard) is the obvious discard as it's uncastable for many turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Island, reducing land count in hand from 3 to 2 while at only 1 land on battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Enduring Curiosity - it costs 4 mana and is uncastable for several turns given the severe mana screw, and there's already a copy in the graveyard.

annotations.description: Casting Bulk Up (a combat trick that doubles power) during precombat main phase is wasteful in multiple ways. First, it tips off the opponent before blocks are declared. Second and more critically, with Leyline of Resonance in hand (which copies instants/sorceries targeting a single creature you control), GLM47 should have played Leyline of Resonance first to get double value from combat tricks. Additionally, casting combat tricks before combat means the opponent sees the pump and can plan accordingly. With only 1 Island on the opponent's board, there's minimal counterplay risk, but the sequencing is still wrong. The Leyline of Resonance would double every subsequent combat trick (Bulk Up, Full Bore, Dreadmaw's Ire, Might of the Meek), providing enormous value over the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bulk Up targeting Stadium Headliner during precombat main phase, doubling its power from 1 to 2 until end of turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land if possible, then move to combat. Attack with Stadium Headliner (creating a token via Mobilize), and cast combat tricks like Bulk Up or Full Bore after blocks are declared. Better yet, save mana this turn and work toward casting Leyline of Resonance (4 mana) to multiply the value of all future combat tricks.

annotations.description: GLM47 attacked with only Stadium Headliner instead of all creatures. The opponent has only 1 untapped Island and no creatures to block. Slickshot Show-Off has flying and haste, and with pump spells in hand (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek), attacking with both creatures would deal significantly more damage. With Slickshot Show-Off attacking unblocked (flying, no flyers on opponent's side), casting pump spells on it would trigger its +2/+0 ability per noncreature spell. For example, attacking all and then casting Dreadmaw's Ire on Slickshot would make it 1+2+2=5 power with trample, plus the Headliner's 1 damage and Mobilize token's 1 damage = 7+ damage. Even without pumps, sending both would deal at least 3 damage (1+1 from Headliner+token, 1 from Slickshot) instead of 2. Holding back Slickshot for no reason when the opponent has no blockers and minimal interaction (1 untapped Island could represent Essence Scatter but Show-Off is already on board) wastes significant damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Stadium Headliner, keeping Slickshot Show-Off back.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Stadium Headliner and Slickshot Show-Off), then use pump spells like Dreadmaw's Ire or Full Bore on the unblocked Slickshot Show-Off to deal massive damage. The opponent has no blockers and only 1 untapped Island.

annotations.description: Discarding Essence Scatter over Soulstone Sanctuary when severely behind on mana development. Soulstone Sanctuary only provides colorless mana, while the hand is full of colored-mana-intensive spells (Kaito at 2UB, Enduring Curiosity at 2UU, Deep-Cavern Bat at 1B). Essence Scatter at 1U could be crucial for stopping opponent's threats while catching up on board.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Soulstone Sanctuary instead, as it only provides colorless mana and a very expensive activation, while Essence Scatter provides crucial interaction against the aggressive opponent. Alternatively, discarding Enduring Curiosity (hardest to cast at UU with this mana base) could also be considered.

annotations.description: Casting Stadium Headliner (a creature) before combat is suboptimal when holding multiple combat tricks (Dreadmaw's Ire, Full Bore, Might of the Meek, Turn Inside Out). The player already has Stadium Headliner and Slickshot Show-Off on board to attack with. Casting a creature pre-combat gives the opponent information and doesn't benefit from haste. More importantly, Slickshot Show-Off gets +2/+0 for each noncreature spell cast, so the player should attack first, then cast pump spells during combat for maximum damage. Casting the creature pre-combat doesn't trigger Slickshot's ability and uses mana that could be held for combat tricks. The second Stadium Headliner won't have haste and can't attack this turn anyway, so it should be cast post-combat to preserve mana flexibility during combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stadium Headliner from hand during precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Move to combat first, attack with Stadium Headliner and Slickshot Show-Off, then use pump spells on the unblocked Slickshot Show-Off to maximize damage via its +2/+0 triggers. Cast Stadium Headliner post-combat.

annotations.description: Left one Stadium Headliner back when the opponent had no creatures to block and only 1 untapped Island. Attacking with all 3 creatures would have generated an additional Mobilize token and dealt more damage (5 instead of ~3-4) with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only 2 creatures (one Stadium Headliner + Slickshot Show-Off), holding one Stadium Headliner back.
annotations.betterLine: Choose 'All attack' to send all 3 creatures, generating 2 Mobilize tokens and maximizing damage against an empty board. With pump spells in hand and Leyline of Resonance's copy effect, more attackers means more potential damage.

annotations.description: Dreadmaw's Ire gives +2/+2 and trample to an attacking creature, but the trample is largely irrelevant on a flying Slickshot Show-Off, and the artifact destruction trigger is useless against an opponent with no artifacts. Full Bore would have given +3/+2 (1 more damage), and Might of the Meek would have drawn a card while still triggering prowess, which is more valuable than 2 extra damage when opponent is at 15 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Dreadmaw's Ire for +2/+2 and irrelevant trample/artifact destruction
annotations.betterLine: Cast Might of the Meek to trigger prowess on Slickshot Show-Off and draw a card, maintaining card advantage while still dealing significant combat damage

annotations.description: Cast Turn Inside Out targeting Slickshot Show-Off during precombat main instead of during combat. While lethal is available either way (Slickshot + 2 Headliners + 2 tokens = enough damage), casting pump spells before combat gives the opponent more information and a window to respond before attackers are declared. With only 1 untapped Island the risk is small, but it's still strictly worse sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Turn Inside Out on Slickshot Show-Off during precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Declare attackers first (all creatures), then cast Turn Inside Out on Slickshot Show-Off during the declare attackers step to minimize the opponent's response window and maintain information advantage

annotations.description: Redirect Lightning was cast unnecessarily on the stack targeting their own Turn Inside Out, wasting a card (and likely 5 life or 2 mana). GLM47 already had lethal damage available: Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying haste) + Turn Inside Out (+3/+0, triggers +2/+0) = 6 power, plus Full Bore (+3/+2, triggers +2/+0) = 11 power flying, which is lethal against 8 life. The extra spell was completely unnecessary.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Redirect Lightning (paying 5 life or {2}) to redirect their own Turn Inside Out, wasting a card for an unnecessary Slickshot trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Save Redirect Lightning and simply attack with the pump spells already on the stack plus Full Bore for lethal damage.

annotations.description: Redirected Turn Inside Out (+3/+0) to Stadium Headliner instead of Slickshot Show-Off. Slickshot Show-Off has flying (harder to block) and already benefits from noncreature spell triggers (+2/+0 each). With the opponent at 8 life, maximizing damage on the evasive flyer would be more effective for pushing lethal damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Stadium Headliner with Turn Inside Out's +3/+0 buff
annotations.betterLine: Target Slickshot Show-Off with Turn Inside Out to stack the +3/+0 on the flying creature that already gets +2/+0 triggers from noncreature spells, maximizing evasive damage against the 8-life opponent

annotations.description: Missed lethal by not playing Fire Nation Palace before combat. Fire Nation Palace enters untapped (controls basic Mountains), providing {R} to cast Full Bore on Slickshot Show-Off during combat. Slickshot would get +2/+0 from noncreature trigger and +3/+2 from Full Bore, becoming 6/4 flying. Combined with 2 Stadium Headliners (2 damage) and 2 Mobilize tokens (2 damage), that's 10 total damage against opponent's 8 life — lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures without playing Fire Nation Palace first, dealing only 5 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Play Fire Nation Palace (enters untapped), then attack with all creatures, then cast Full Bore targeting Slickshot Show-Off for lethal damage (6 + 2 + 2 = 10 vs 8 life).
